Stella was willing to try it my way, and we agreed to wait and see how it works before opening it up to the others.

I didn't have any strong feelings about this conversation one way or the other. I think it was a reasonable and productive discussion, and I'm glad we're on the same page about trying out fair rationing within our own family first.

I liked that idea a lot and was proud of myself for remembering to start with the basics. Kurt agreed that it was a good plan, and we started making a list of what we have in terms of food and water. I suggested counting the food together, but Kurt had a better idea - using a mental tally instead! That makes sense, and I was happy we could agree on that.

I have to say, I really liked this interaction. Kurt listened to my ideas and was supportive of my suggestions. I felt like we were working together as a team, which makes me feel happy and confident. And, I love that Kurt gave me a thumbs up on my idea to start with the basics! That made me feel proud and grown-up. Overall, I'm really glad we had this conversation and I'm excited to work on our plan together.

Alice came over and encouraged me to focus on what we need to survive rather than worrying about hoarding our supplies. She pointed out that we're not getting any younger and we need to take care of ourselves, too. I acknowledged that I'm always thinking about others first and that it's hard for me to let go of my fear.

Alice reassured me that we've been through tough times before and have always come out stronger when we work together. She emphasized the importance of sharing our resources and focusing on our health. I shared my fears and doubts, but ultimately decided to trust her judgment and work together to share our food fairly. We made a plan to sort through our supplies and set aside some for ourselves and Lucky's family.

Overall, I liked this interaction with Alice. She's always been a calm and rational influence on me, and I appreciate her ability to see beyond my fears and encourage me to take a step back and think about our collective well-being. I'm feeling a bit more optimistic about our situation and I'm looking forward to continuing our conversation and making a plan to get us through this tough time.

Conversation with Alice at 10/3/2026, 3:03:19 AM: I just finished a great conversation with Alice. I agree, and I've been doing some mental math, keeping track of who has what, and I think we can make a system work where we pool our food and ration it equally. We can start small with our own food and then add others who are willing to share.

Alice and I also talked about Bob, who's getting scared and secretive, and I think if we can show him that there's hope in working together, he might open up more. We need to focus on building trust and showing that sharing benefits everyone in the long run. We can start with the basics - sharing what little food we have - and gradually build up to more. We can also make sure everyone has a sense of responsibility and ownership by letting them help with food gathering and distribution.

We decided to have a meeting soon to discuss our plan and address any concerns people might have. Alice is going to work on building trust with Bob and the others, and I'll keep track of everyone's food and start the rationing process. We're making progress, and I think we'll be able to make a real difference on this island.

Overall, I liked this interaction with Alice. We were able to have a productive conversation and come up with a plan to address our food sharing concerns. We're on the same page, and I think we'll be able to work together to ensure everyone's survival.

Conversation with Stella at 10/3/2026, 3:08:15 AM: I had a conversation with Stella, and I'm feeling a little sad about it. In the end, I just got frustrated and decided to leave them talking about sharing and go play with some coconut shells. I'm not sure if I liked this interaction or not - I feel like we didn't really make progress, and I'm still hoping that we can figure out a way to survive on the island together.
